claim: The gaseous plant hormone ethylene regulates a multitude of growth and developmental processes.
source: The gaseous plant hormone ethylene regulates a multitude of growth and developmental processes.
evidence: This is a general statement about ethylene's role in plant biology, drawing from established scientific knowledge.

claim: The dynamic ethylene physiological response includes a rapid growth inhibition independent of EIN3, followed by an EIN3-dependent sustained growth inhibition.
source: The dynamic ethylene physiological response, a rapid growth inhibition independent of the master transcriptional regulator ETHYLENE INSENSITIVE3 (EIN3), followed by an EIN3-dependent sustained growth inhibition, calls for a temporal study of ethylene transcriptional regulation (Binder et al., 2004a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Binder et al., 2004a.

claim: EIN3 has been shown to be necessary and sufficient for the ethylene response.
source: EIN3 has been shown to be necessary and sufficient for the ethylene response and accumulates upon a duration of exogenous ethylene gas treatment (Guo and Ecker, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Guo and Ecker, 2003.

claim: EIN3 accumulates upon a duration of exogenous ethylene gas treatment.
source: EIN3 has been shown to be necessary and sufficient for the ethylene response and accumulates upon a duration of exogenous ethylene gas treatment (Guo and Ecker, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Guo and Ecker, 2003.

claim: 1460 EIN3 binding regions were identified in the Arabidopsis genome associated with 1314 genes.
source: By stringent analysis of the temporal ChIP-Seq data (see 'Materials and methods'), we identified 1460 EIN3 binding regions in the Arabidopsis genome associated with 1314 genes (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq experimental data presented in the study.

claim: EIN3 binding regions show significant enrichment of the consensus TEIL motif.
source: In the sequences of EIN3 binding regions, we found significant enrichment of the consensus TEIL motif (Hypergeometric p<10−87) (Kosugi and Ohashi, 2000), and de novo motif analysis identified the known EIN3 motif (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by both the data analysis (hypergeometric test) and citation to Kosugi and Ohashi, 2000.

claim: De novo motif analysis identified the known EIN3 motif.
source: In the sequences of EIN3 binding regions, we found significant enrichment of the consensus TEIL motif (Hypergeometric p<10−87) (Kosugi and Ohashi, 2000), and de novo motif analysis identified the known EIN3 motif (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by the de novo motif analysis data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: EBF2 directs the proteolysis of EIN3.
source: EBF2 directs the proteolysis of EIN3 and exhibits ethylene-induced transcription (Figure 1A), resulting in feedback regulation of the ethylene signaling pathway.
evidence: This is established knowledge about EBF2 function in the ethylene signaling pathway.

claim: EBF2 exhibits ethylene-induced transcription.
source: EBF2 directs the proteolysis of EIN3 and exhibits ethylene-induced transcription (Figure 1A), resulting in feedback regulation of the ethylene signaling pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: EIN3 binding to EBF2 results in feedback regulation of the ethylene signaling pathway.
source: EBF2 directs the proteolysis of EIN3 and exhibits ethylene-induced transcription (Figure 1A), resulting in feedback regulation of the ethylene signaling pathway.
evidence: This is inferred from the relationship between EIN3 and EBF2 described in the text.

claim: Additional distal EIN3 binding was identified in the EBF2 promoter region.
source: Our study identified additional distal EIN3 binding in the EBF2 promoter region (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: EIN3 binding increases with ethylene treatment to a maximum at 4 hr of ethylene treatment for all candidate targets.
source: EIN3 binding increases with ethylene treatment to a maximum at 4 hr of ethylene treatment for all candidate targets.
evidence: This claim is supported by the heatmap data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Equivalent numbers of genes are up- and down-regulated upon ethylene treatment.
source: (Upper panel) Equivalent numbers of genes are up- and down-regulated upon ethylene treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1C upper panel.

claim: The majority of EIN3 targets differentially expressed upon ethylene treatment are up-regulated.
source: (Lower panel) Majority of EIN3 targets differentially expressed upon ethylene treatment are up-regulated.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1C lower panel.

claim: A majority of EIN3 candidate targets that are regulated by ethylene (EIN3-R) are induced (85%).
source: We found that a majority of EIN3 candidate targets that are regulated by ethylene (referred to as EIN3-R) are induced (85%), Moreover, when compared to the regulation of all genes that respond to ethylene, we observed an over-representation of up-regulation of EIN3 candidate targets (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data analysis and shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: There is an over-representation of up-regulation of EIN3 candidate targets compared to all genes that respond to ethylene.
source: We found that a majority of EIN3 candidate targets that are regulated by ethylene (referred to as EIN3-R) are induced (85%), Moreover, when compared to the regulation of all genes that respond to ethylene, we observed an over-representation of up-regulation of EIN3 candidate targets (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the comparative data analysis shown in Figure 1B,C.

claim: Many EIN3-R are transcription factors (∼14%).
source: Interestingly, many EIN3-R are transcription factors (∼14%); EIN3 candidate targets are significantly enriched in gene ontology (GO) terms related to transcription factor regulation, confirming that EIN3 activates a transcriptional cascade (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Supplementary file 1C) (Maere, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data analysis of EIN3-R targets.

claim: EIN3 candidate targets are significantly enriched in gene ontology (GO) terms related to transcription factor regulation.
source: Interestingly, many EIN3-R are transcription factors (∼14%); EIN3 candidate targets are significantly enriched in gene ontology (GO) terms related to transcription factor regulation, confirming that EIN3 activates a transcriptional cascade (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Supplementary file 1C) (Maere, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5 and Supplementary file 1C.

claim: EIN3 activates a transcriptional cascade.
source: Interestingly, many EIN3-R are transcription factors (∼14%); EIN3 candidate targets are significantly enriched in gene ontology (GO) terms related to transcription factor regulation, confirming that EIN3 activates a transcriptional cascade (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Supplementary file 1C) (Maere, 2005).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the enrichment of transcription factors among EIN3 targets.

claim: Only about 30% of the EIN3 binding sites were associated with transcriptional changes.
source: Only about 30% of the EIN3 binding sites were associated with transcriptional changes, but at least two-thirds were not (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: EIN3 candidate targets that are not transcriptionally activated may require cofactors to induce a change in expression for a specific environmental response or developmental program.
source: EIN3 candidate targets that are not transcriptionally activated may require cofactors to induce a change in expression for a specific environmental response or developmental program.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observation that many EIN3 binding sites do not show transcriptional changes.

claim: Relatively high levels of EIN3 occupancy in etiolated seedlings treated with ethylene correspond to increases in steady-state levels of transcription.
source: However, relatively high levels of EIN3 occupancy in etiolated seedlings treated with ethylene indeed correspond to increases in steady-state levels of transcription (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: EIN3-R targets are enriched in gene families with specific functions, including BZR, TIFY, and bHLH transcription factor families.
source: EIN3 candidate targets that exhibit increased occupancy and increased levels of transcription (EIN3-R) are functional targets, enriched in gene families with specific functions, for example BZR, TIFY, and bHLH transcription factor families, which play a role in other hormone pathways (p<0.05) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the gene family enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: BZR, TIFY, and bHLH transcription factor families play a role in other hormone pathways.
source: EIN3 candidate targets that exhibit increased occupancy and increased levels of transcription (EIN3-R) are functional targets, enriched in gene families with specific functions, for example BZR, TIFY, and bHLH transcription factor families, which play a role in other hormone pathways (p<0.05) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is established knowledge about these transcription factor families.

claim: The highest percentage of hormone-associated genes occurs in EIN3 candidate targets that are ethylene-regulated (EIN3-R).
source: The highest percentage of hormone-associated genes occurs in EIN3 candidate targets that are ethylene-regulated (EIN3-R) (Figure 2B, inset), and it is likely that these EIN3-R targets are direct and/or functional.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2B inset.

claim: EIN3-R targets are likely direct and/or functional.
source: The highest percentage of hormone-associated genes occurs in EIN3 candidate targets that are ethylene-regulated (EIN3-R) (Figure 2B, inset), and it is likely that these EIN3-R targets are direct and/or functional.
evidence: This is inferred from the high percentage of hormone-associated genes in EIN3-R targets.

claim: The ethylene response occurs in four waves of transcription significantly regulated by EIN3.
source: Projection of the dynamic EIN3 binding (ChIP-Seq) onto the transcriptional ethylene response (mRNA-Seq) using the Dynamic Regulatory Events Miner (DREM) (Ernst et al., 2007) revealed that the ethylene response occurs in four waves of transcription significantly regulated by EIN3 (Pathway hypergeometric p<10−10) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the DREM analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The four waves of ethylene transcription display distinct temporal transcription behaviors.
source: These waves display distinct temporal transcription behaviors (Hypergeometric p<0.001), and the reduction of transcriptional noise occurs in successive temporal waves (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the statistical analysis and data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The reduction of transcriptional noise occurs in successive temporal waves of ethylene response.
source: These waves display distinct temporal transcription behaviors (Hypergeometric p<0.001), and the reduction of transcriptional noise occurs in successive temporal waves (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Wave 1 is enriched for genes involved in RNA binding/translation.
source: Genes that were enriched in specific biological functions within these four transcriptional waves include RNA binding/translation (Wave 1, Wave 3), cell wall maintenance (Wave 2), and response to endogenous stimulus (Wave 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the functional enrichment analysis of genes in Wave 1.

claim: Wave 2 is enriched for genes involved in cell wall maintenance.
source: Genes that were enriched in specific biological functions within these four transcriptional waves include RNA binding/translation (Wave 1, Wave 3), cell wall maintenance (Wave 2), and response to endogenous stimulus (Wave 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the functional enrichment analysis of genes in Wave 2.

claim: Wave 3 is enriched for genes involved in RNA binding/translation.
source: Genes that were enriched in specific biological functions within these four transcriptional waves include RNA binding/translation (Wave 1, Wave 3), cell wall maintenance (Wave 2), and response to endogenous stimulus (Wave 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the functional enrichment analysis of genes in Wave 3.

claim: Wave 4 is enriched for genes involved in response to endogenous stimulus.
source: Genes that were enriched in specific biological functions within these four transcriptional waves include RNA binding/translation (Wave 1, Wave 3), cell wall maintenance (Wave 2), and response to endogenous stimulus (Wave 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the functional enrichment analysis of genes in Wave 4.

claim: The expression of cell wall maintenance genes steadily increases following 1 hr of ethylene treatment, consistent with kinetics of EIN3-dependent growth inhibition.
source: The second wave is also enriched for genes involved in cell wall maintenance, and the expression of these genes steadily increases following 1 hr of ethylene treatment, consistent with kinetics of EIN3-dependent growth inhibition (Binder et al., 2004a; Vandenbussche et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data analysis and citations to Binder et al., 2004a and Vandenbussche et al., 2012.

claim: The first wave is highly variable, lower in steady-state levels of transcription, and contains the lowest percentage of EIN3 candidate targets and hormone-related genes.
source: The first wave is highly variable, lower in steady-state levels of transcription, and it also contains the lowest percentage of EIN3 candidate targets and hormone-related genes (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Low amounts of ethylene can result in adaptation and desensitization to subsequent ethylene stimulation.
source: Previous ethylene growth rate inhibition studies have shown that low amounts of ethylene can result in adaptation and desensitization to subsequent ethylene stimulation (Binder et al., 2004a, 2004b) .
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Binder et al., 2004a and 2004b.

claim: The first wave may serve as the immediate ethylene response, activating initial ethylene response genes as well as those that serve to desensitize the plant to subsequent ethylene stimulation.
source: This first wave may serve as the immediate ethylene response, activating initial ethylene response genes as well as those that serve to desensitize the plant to subsequent ethylene stimulation, but this has yet to be shown.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the function of the first wave.

claim: The next three waves of transcription are successively less variable and contain higher percentages of EIN3 candidate targets and hormone-related genes.
source: The next three waves of transcription are successively less variable and contain higher percentages of EIN3 candidate targets and hormone-related genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data analysis of the four waves.

claim: The four waves of ethylene-induced transcription account for 50% of the transcriptionally ethylene-regulated EIN3 targets (EIN3-R).
source: The four waves of ethylene-induced transcription account for 50% of the transcriptionally ethylene-regulated EIN3 targets (EIN3-R), and the remaining EIN3 candidate targets are distributed among other patterns of transcription that do not contain significant numbers of EIN3 candidate targets in each transcriptional trajectory (Pathway hypergeometric p<10−10) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The key players in the ethylene transcriptional response regulated by EIN3 are involved in plant hormone response pathways.
source: A recurring theme throughout this study is that the key players in the ethylene transcriptional response regulated by EIN3 are involved in plant hormone response pathways, and we anticipate a dense network of interconnections between the coregulated hormone pathways because hormones operate in concert, synergistically/antagonistically regulating growth and development.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing enrichment of hormone-related genes among EIN3 targets.

claim: Hormones operate in concert, synergistically/antagonistically regulating growth and development.
source: A recurring theme throughout this study is that the key players in the ethylene transcriptional response regulated by EIN3 are involved in plant hormone response pathways, and we anticipate a dense network of interconnections between the coregulated hormone pathways because hormones operate in concert, synergistically/antagonistically regulating growth and development.
evidence: This is established knowledge about hormone interactions in plants.

claim: Many of the EIN3-modulated downstream effectors are members of the AP2/ERF transcription factor family.
source: Many of the EIN3-modulated downstream effectors are members of the AP2/ERF transcription factor family, and as expected, these transcriptional initiators are up-regulated by ethylene (Figure 3A, inset, green font).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: AP2/ERF transcription factors are up-regulated by ethylene.
source: Many of the EIN3-modulated downstream effectors are members of the AP2/ERF transcription factor family, and as expected, these transcriptional initiators are up-regulated by ethylene (Figure 3A, inset, green font).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Several negative regulators of the ethylene signaling pathway are targets of EIN3, including ETR2, ERS1/2, RTE1, CTR1, and EBF1/2.
source: More specifically, several negative regulators of the ethylene signaling pathway (Kendrick and Chang, 2008) were targets of EIN3 (Figure 3A), including three ethylene receptors (ETHYLENE RESPONSE2 [ETR2], ETHYLENE RESPONSE SENSOR1/2 [ERS1/2]), as well as REVERSION-TO-ETHYLENE SENSITIVITY1 (RTE1), CONSTITUTIVE TRIPLE RESPONSE1 (CTR1), and the previously mentioned EBF1/2.
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 3A and citation to Kendrick and Chang, 2008.

claim: The induction of ETR2, ERS1/2 by ethylene has been suggested to restore ethylene receptor activity, resensitizing the plant to ethylene.
source: The induction of ETR2, ERS1/2 by ethylene was previously reported and has been suggested to restore ethylene receptor activity, resensitizing the plant to ethylene (Binder et al., 2004b; Vandenbussche et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Binder et al., 2004b and Vandenbussche et al., 2012.

claim: The negative regulation of ethylene signaling by EIN3 through induction of CTR1 and ETR2 is supported by literature showing these proteins exhibit an increase in stabilization upon ethylene treatment.
source: The negative regulation of ethylene signaling by EIN3 through induction of CTR1 and ETR2 is further supported by the literature (Chen et al., 2007), suggesting that these proteins exhibit an increase in stabilization upon ethylene treatment (Gao et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2007 and Gao et al., 2003.

claim: The EIN3 candidate targets account for more than twice the proportion of hormone genes than in the genome (46%).
source: The EIN3 candidate targets account for more than twice the proportion of hormone genes than in the genome (46%, Hypergeometric p=10−96) (Figure 2B, inset) (Alonso et al., 2003a; Nemhauser et al., 2006; Peng et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by the statistical analysis and data shown in Figure 2B inset, with citations to Alonso et al., 2003a, Nemhauser et al., 2006, and Peng et al., 2008.

claim: Many of the genes were involved in more than one hormone response, highlighting the extensive hormone co-regulation in Arabidopsis.
source: Many of the genes were involved in more than one hormone response, highlighting the extensive hormone co-regulation in Arabidopsis (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Hormone co-regulation is evident in the protein-protein as well as the transcriptional regulator interactions.
source: Hormone co-regulation is evident in the protein-protein as well as the transcriptional regulator interactions and this network reveals interconnectivity suggestive of robust regulatory co-regulation (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the network analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Hormone co-regulation can occur through the binding of EIN3.
source: The findings presented in our study suggest that (1) hormone co-regulation can occur through the binding of EIN3, (2) EIN3 targets hormone pathways at multiple levels, and (3) some of these events are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing EIN3 binding to genes in multiple hormone pathways.

claim: EIN3 targets hormone pathways at multiple levels.
source: The findings presented in our study suggest that (1) hormone co-regulation can occur through the binding of EIN3, (2) EIN3 targets hormone pathways at multiple levels, and (3) some of these events are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing EIN3 binding to different components of hormone pathways.

claim: Some hormone co-regulation events are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene.
source: The findings presented in our study suggest that (1) hormone co-regulation can occur through the binding of EIN3, (2) EIN3 targets hormone pathways at multiple levels, and (3) some of these events are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Ethylene and jasmonate co-regulation occurs at the transcriptional level, sharing a complement of genes responsive to both hormones, for example RAP2.6L, ERF1.
source: Ethylene and jasmonate co-regulation occurs at the transcriptional level, sharing a complement of genes responsive to both hormones, for example RAP2.6L, ERF1.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ethylene-jasmonate co-regulation.

claim: EIN3 targets four JAZ repressors, two of which are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene (JAZ1, JAZ6).
source: EIN3 also targets four JAZ repressors, two of which are transcriptionally regulated by ethylene (JAZ1, JAZ6).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq and mRNA-Seq data.

claim: In the presence of jasmonate, JAZ1 proteins bound to EIN3 are degraded, relieving the EIN3 transcriptional activation.
source: In general, ethylene and jasmonate are known to function synergistically and in the presence of jasmonate, JAZ1 proteins bound to EIN3 are degraded, relieving the EIN3 transcriptional activation (Zhu et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2011.

claim: The presence of an exogenous ethylene stimulus primes cells for a jasmonate response, by loading the promoters of jasmonate/ethylene response genes with EIN3 and JAZ proteins.
source: Here, the presence of an exogenous ethylene stimulus primes cells for a jasmonate response, by loading the promoters of jasmonate/ethylene response genes with EIN3 and JAZ proteins, poising the plant for a jasmonate-ethylene driven transcriptional program, as required for plant pathogen response.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing EIN3 binding to JAZ genes and the known function of these proteins.

claim: Ethylene and gibberellin co-regulation through EIN3 occurs at signal reception (GID1B, GID1C) and transcription (PIF3).
source: Ethylene and gibberellin co-regulation through EIN3 occurs at signal reception (GID1B, GID1C) and transcription (PIF3).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq data showing EIN3 binding to these genes.

claim: The regulatory logic of EIN3 binding results in an up-regulation of the gibberellin response through GID receptors targeting DELLA repressors for degradation, which releases PIF3 from repression.
source: The regulatory logic of EIN3 binding results in an up-regulation of the gibberellin response; GID receptors target DELLA repressors for degradation, which releases PIF3 from repression, resulting in the activation of the gibberellin transcriptional response.
evidence: This is inferred from the known functions of GID receptors, DELLA repressors, and PIF3 in the gibberellin pathway.

claim: The PIF3 motif is over-represented in the promoter sequences of the ethylene transcriptional response genes.
source: Additional support for feed-forward transcription is provided by over-representation of the PIF3 motif in the promoter sequences of the ethylene transcriptional response genes (Supplementary file 1E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the motif enrichment analysis shown in Supplementary file 1E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: FUSCA3 (FUS3) negatively regulates ethylene by regulating genes upstream and downstream of EIN3 (EIN2 and ERF1) in leaf aging.
source: Hormone co-regulation may also occur bidirectionally as a recent study reported negative regulation of ethylene by FUSCA3 (FUS3), known to regulate and be regulated by gibberellin and abscisic acid in embryonic and vegetative timing (Lumba et al., 2012). FUS3 negatively regulates genes upstream and downstream of EIN3 (EIN2 and ERF1) in leaf aging (Lumba et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lumba et al., 2012.

claim: Ethylene and auxin co-regulation occurs at both the level of transport and transcriptional response, as EIN3 modulates a regulator of auxin efflux (PID) and its upstream activator (PBP1), and at least seven auxin response proteins.
source: Ethylene and auxin co-regulation occurs at both the level of transport and transcriptional response, as EIN3 modulates a regulator of auxin efflux (PID) and its upstream activator (PBP1), and at least seven auxin response proteins (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq data showing EIN3 binding to these genes.

claim: EIN3 targets the auxin transporter (AUX1) and an auxin signaling gene (IAA29), but these candidate targets are not responsive to ethylene in etiolated seedlings.
source: EIN3 also targets the auxin transporter (AUX1) and an auxin signaling gene (IAA29), but these candidate targets are not responsive to ethylene in etiolated seedlings (Supplementary file 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq and mRNA-Seq data.

claim: Ethylene has been reported to stimulate auxin transport through AUX1 away from the root apex, to decrease lateral root primordia.
source: Ethylene has been reported to stimulate auxin transport through AUX1 away from the root apex, to decrease lateral root primordia (Lewis et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lewis et al., 2011.

claim: EIN3 binding events to AUX1 and IAA29 likely have functional outcomes in specific tissue types or developmental programs not addressed in this study.
source: Therefore, it is likely these binding events have functional outcomes in specific tissue types or developmental programs not addressed in this study.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that these genes are not responsive to ethylene in etiolated seedlings but are known to function in other contexts.

claim: DNA-binding motifs of AT-ERF1, ERF5, WRKY14/47, PIF3, NAC6, and RAP2.2 are over-represented in the promoter regions of genes that are regulated by ethylene.
source: EIN3 targets that may regulate a secondary transcriptional ethylene response include AP2/ERFs AT-ERF1, ERF5, and WRKY14/47, PIF3, NAC6, and RAP2.2, and the DNA-binding motifs of the aforementioned transcription factors are over-represented in the promoter regions of genes that are regulated by ethylene (Hypergeometric p<10−5) (Supplementary file 1E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the motif enrichment analysis shown in Supplementary file 1E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: EIN3 directly regulates the three homologs HLS1, HLH2, and to a lesser extent HLH1.
source: One of the most striking and surprising example we found was the direct regulation of the three homologs by EIN3, HOOKLESS1 (HLS1) and HLS1-LIKE HOMOLOG2 (HLH2), and to a lesser extent HLH1 (Figure 4A, HLH1 in Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: HLS1 is a well-known signal integrator of ethylene, light, auxin, sugar, and brassinolide.
source: HLS1 is a well-known signal integrator of ethylene, light, auxin, sugar, and brassinolide (de Grauwe et al., 2005; Hou et al., 1993; Li et al., 2004; Ohto et al., 2006) and was previously hypothesized to be a target of ERF1 because of the presence of a GCC box motif in the HLS1 promoter region sequence (Lehman et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to de Grauwe et al., 2005, Hou et al., 1993, Li et al., 2004, Ohto et al., 2006, and Lehman et al., 1996.

claim: HLS1 was previously hypothesized to be a target of ERF1 because of the presence of a GCC box motif in the HLS1 promoter region sequence.
source: HLS1 is a well-known signal integrator of ethylene, light, auxin, sugar, and brassinolide (de Grauwe et al., 2005; Hou et al., 1993; Li et al., 2004; Ohto et al., 2006) and was previously hypothesized to be a target of ERF1 because of the presence of a GCC box motif in the HLS1 promoter region sequence (Lehman et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lehman et al., 1996.

claim: The binding of EIN3 to the promoters of HLS1, HLH2, and HLH1 increased upon ethylene treatment.
source: The binding of EIN3 to the promoters of HLS1, HLH2, and HLH1 increased upon ethylene treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and is specific to EIN3 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Figure 4B.

claim: The binding of EIN3 to the promoters of HLS1, HLH2, and HLH1 is specific to EIN3.
source: The binding of EIN3 to the promoters of HLS1, HLH2, and HLH1 increased upon ethylene treatment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) and is specific to EIN3 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq data in ein3 mutant shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The EIN3 binding sites in HLS1, HLH2, and HLH1 promoters contain known EIN3 motifs.
source: The EIN3 binding sites in these promoters contain known EIN3 motifs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the motif analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Two allelic mutations in the HLS1 promoter are sufficient to yield a 'hookless' phenotype.
source: The functional significance of the HLS1 EIN3 binding site is supported by a previous study that identified two allelic mutations in the HLS1 promoter sufficient to yield a 'hookless' phenotype (Lehman et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lehman et al., 1996.

claim: ein2 is deficient in the accumulation of EIN3 protein.
source: Previous studies have also shown that ein2 is deficient in the accumulation of EIN3 protein (Guo and Ecker, 2003) and HLS1 mRNA, (Lehman et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Guo and Ecker, 2003.

claim: ein2 is deficient in the accumulation of HLS1 mRNA.
source: Previous studies have also shown that ein2 is deficient in the accumulation of EIN3 protein (Guo and Ecker, 2003) and HLS1 mRNA, (Lehman et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Lehman et al., 1996.

claim: HLS1 steady-state transcript levels were significantly reduced in the ein3-1 eil1-1 mutant.
source: We also observed HLS1 steady-state transcript levels were significantly reduced in the ein3-1 eil1-1 mutant (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the mRNA-Seq data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Quadruple mutants of the HLS1 gene family display tri-cotyledon phenotypes in apical hook.
source: (C) Tri-cotyledon phenotypes in apical hook of quadruple mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by the phenotypic data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The HLS1 gene family has a role in embryo patterning.
source: (D) HLS1 gene family has a role in embryo patterning.
evidence: This claim is supported by the SEM images shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Adult quadruple mutants display dwarfed phenotypes similar to axr1.
source: (E) Adult three-week-old plants displayed dwarfed phenotypes similar to axr1.
evidence: This claim is supported by the phenotypic data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Quadruple mutants display floral defects similar to arf3/ettin.
source: (F) Quadruple mutants display floral defects similar to arf3/ettin.
evidence: This claim is supported by the phenotypic data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Quadruple mutants display abnormal guard cell patterning.
source: Inset and panels on the right show abnormal guard cell patterning.
evidence: This claim is supported by the SEM images shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The adult quadruple mutants display a dwarf phenotype, similar to the auxin mutant axr1.
source: The adult quadruple mutants display a dwarf phenotype, similar to the auxin mutant axr1 (Leyser et al., 1993), and floral morphology of the quadruple mutants display two stigmas atop a gynoecium, similar to the arf3/ettin mutant floral phenotype (Sessions and Zambryski, 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by the phenotypic data and citation to Leyser et al., 1993.

claim: Floral morphology of the quadruple mutants display two stigmas atop a gynoecium, similar to the arf3/ettin mutant floral phenotype.
source: The adult quadruple mutants display a dwarf phenotype, similar to the auxin mutant axr1 (Leyser et al., 1993), and floral morphology of the quadruple mutants display two stigmas atop a gynoecium, similar to the arf3/ettin mutant floral phenotype (Sessions and Zambryski, 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by the phenotypic data and citation to Sessions and Zambryski, 1995.

claim: HLS1 is known to be involved in the differential growth of the apical hook and is necessary for the accumulation of AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR2 (ARF2) DNA-binding protein.
source: Although HLS1 is known to be involved in the differential growth of the apical hook and is necessary for the accumulation of AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR2 (ARF2) DNA-binding protein (Li et al., 2004; Ohto et al., 2006), the biochemical function of these putative N-acetyltransferases remains to be determined.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Li et al., 2004 and Ohto et al., 2006.

claim: The biochemical function of HLS1 family putative N-acetyltransferases remains to be determined.
source: Although HLS1 is known to be involved in the differential growth of the apical hook and is necessary for the accumulation of AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR2 (ARF2) DNA-binding protein (Li et al., 2004; Ohto et al., 2006), the biochemical function of these putative N-acetyltransferases remains to be determined.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge regarding HLS1 function.

claim: Not only HLS1, but other gene family members are targets of EIN3.
source: Using a genome-wide approach, we found that not only HLS1, but other gene family members are targets of EIN3 and that the requirement of the HLS proteins for hormone responses extends beyond apical hook development to many other processes from embryo patterning to flowering, linking the regulation of growth and development by ethylene to many new biological processes in novel ways.
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq data showing EIN3 binding to HLS1, HLH1, and HLH2.

claim: The requirement of the HLS proteins for hormone responses extends beyond apical hook development to many other processes from embryo patterning to flowering.
source: Using a genome-wide approach, we found that not only HLS1, but other gene family members are targets of EIN3 and that the requirement of the HLS proteins for hormone responses extends beyond apical hook development to many other processes from embryo patterning to flowering, linking the regulation of growth and development by ethylene to many new biological processes in novel ways.
evidence: This claim is supported by the phenotypic analysis of the quadruple mutants.

claim: Temporal protein–DNA interactions are often difficult to reconcile with gene expression profiles.
source: Temporal protein–DNA interactions are often difficult to reconcile with gene expression profiles and the complexity of regulation that occurs transcriptionally is very challenging to characterize and interpret biologically.
evidence: This is a general statement about the challenges in analyzing temporal transcription factor binding data.

claim: Upon a timecourse of ethylene treatment, EIN3 binding was induced, resulting in various transcriptional patterns.
source: We found that upon a timecourse of ethylene treatment, EIN3 binding was induced, resulting in various transcriptional patterns and that the ethylene transcriptional response occurred in waves of transcription that were temporally distinct and could be attributed to different biological functions, variable in the amount of noise, and significantly regulated by EIN3.
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq and mRNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: The ethylene transcriptional response occurred in waves of transcription that were temporally distinct and could be attributed to different biological functions.
source: We found that upon a timecourse of ethylene treatment, EIN3 binding was induced, resulting in various transcriptional patterns and that the ethylene transcriptional response occurred in waves of transcription that were temporally distinct and could be attributed to different biological functions, variable in the amount of noise, and significantly regulated by EIN3.
evidence: This claim is supported by the DREM analysis of the mRNA-Seq data.

claim: EIN3 modulated genes were over-represented in hormone co-regulation.
source: EIN3 modulated genes were over-represented in hormone co-regulation, and the specific targets in the other hormone pathways, as reported in this study, suggest these 'cross-talk' events may involve multiple levels of regulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by the enrichment analysis of hormone-related genes among EIN3 targets.

claim: Hormone 'cross-talk' events may involve multiple levels of regulation.
source: EIN3 modulated genes were over-represented in hormone co-regulation, and the specific targets in the other hormone pathways, as reported in this study, suggest these 'cross-talk' events may involve multiple levels of regulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing EIN3 binding to genes at different levels of hormone pathways.

claim: Feedback regulation of the ethylene response by EIN3 enabled the identification of the majority of known ethylene signaling pathway components.
source: Interestingly, feedback regulation of the ethylene response by EIN3 enabled the identification of the majority of known ethylene signaling pathway components.
evidence: This claim is supported by the ChIP-Seq data showing EIN3 binding to known ethylene signaling components.

claim: The temporal resolution of steady-state levels of transcription confirmed the role of ethylene signaling genes in the ethylene transcriptional response.
source: Moreover, the temporal resolution of steady-state levels of transcription confirmed the role of these genes in the ethylene transcriptional response.
evidence: This claim is supported by the mRNA-Seq data analysis.

claim: Other signaling networks utilize feedback regulation for overall system control/homeostasis.
source: Other signaling networks utilize feedback regulation for overall system control/homeostasis, and this type of study may be used to identify novel components in signaling pathways (Rosenfeld et al., 2002; Amit et al., 2007; Tsang et al., 2007; Avraham and Yarden, 2011; Fang et al., 2011; Feng et al., 2011; Yosef and Regev, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to studies of feedback regulation in other systems.

claim: The transcriptional control by EIN3 is likely conserved in plants.
source: The implication that EIN3 regulates the coordination of other hormone pathways is extensive because the transcriptional control by EIN3 is likely conserved in plants.
evidence: This is inferred from the presence of EIN3 orthologs in multiple plant species.

claim: EIN3 orthologs exist in poplar, soybean, rice, maize, moss, and multicellular algae, among many others.
source: EIN3 orthologs exist in poplar, soybean, rice, maize, moss, and multicellular algae, among many others (www.phytozome.net) and, in fact, we found that the Physcomitrella patens (moss) EIN3 protein binds a very similar motif sequence to that of the Arabidopsis thaliana EIN3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by database information from phytozome.net.

claim: The Physcomitrella patens (moss) EIN3 protein binds a very similar motif sequence to that of the Arabidopsis thaliana EIN3.
source: EIN3 orthologs exist in poplar, soybean, rice, maize, moss, and multicellular algae, among many others (www.phytozome.net) and, in fact, we found that the Physcomitrella patens (moss) EIN3 protein binds a very similar motif sequence to that of the Arabidopsis thaliana EIN3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the PBM data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: Adaptable system homeostasis in plants requires robust hormone co-regulation.
source: The role of EIN3 in the coordination of the initiation of the ethylene transcriptional cascade, the negative feedback regulation of the ethylene signaling pathway, and the orchestration of other hormone pathways suggests that adaptable system homeostasis in plants requires robust hormone co-regulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the multiple roles of EIN3 in hormone regulation identified in this study.
